newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African industrial shares launched a late rally on Thursday to end in positive territory on the back of hopes Wall Street may soon make a come back, dealers said.
The recovery recouped opening losses on all the major indices after New York shares posted an overnight loss that restarted its recent correction.
Dealers said South African shares were joining in the herd mentality of most other major financial markets and waiting on U.S. shares' every move.
"All around the world everything is dominated by Wall Street at the moment," said Johan Marais, a director at Societe Generale Frankel Pollak.
The industrials index added 22.5 points to 8,202.3 as the all-share index ended unmoved at 6,981.1.
Continuing a pattern set at the start of the week individual blue chip share performances were mixed with Iscor ending down six cents to 346 cents and Richemont finishing up 25 cents to 57.50 rand.

There was a modestly healthy volume of about 619 million rands worth of shares being traded amidst good underlying institutional demand and some selective bargain hunting after the sell-off at the start of the week.

But some dealers said that there was no guarantee the Dow would rise in its next session with an expected sell-off in IBM set to weigh on the market. Reports have recently suggested analysts have slimmed down their earnings forecasts for the computer giant.

They added South African shares are likely to remain vulnerable to any U.S. inspired nervousness with all market eyes watching Friday's U.S. employment data due out on Friday for hints on the speed of growth in the U.S. economy.
Gold shares had another dull day, sinking early on bullion woes as European prices for the yellow metal sank below the psychologically important $350 an ounce level.
The index ended down 8.5 points to 1,289.0 after failing to join in the recovery enjoyed by industrials.
"The gold index has been very quiet. People are just staying away," said one dealer.
Dealers added that if Wall Steet's stranglehold on the market breaks soon, then market eyes could focus once again on gold shares and put them under further selling pressure.
South African share futures began weak but also launched a recovery and to last trade comfortably up.
The all-share June contract was at 6,387/400 from 6,365 as the industrials contract wast at 7,960/970 from 7,927. The golds contract was off to 895/906 from 915.
